title: Generic crystallization and nucleation
text: Crystallization commonly becomes visually observable when nuclei or crystals appear and solid-region area/count begins to increase. Cooling or solvent composition changes can reduce solubility and promote supersaturation. Visual evidence alone does not identify the compound, so material identity and conditions are needed for chemical interpretation.

title: Benzoic acid crystallization from water
text: Benzoic acid has temperature-dependent solubility in water and is commonly crystallized by dissolving at elevated temperature and cooling. During cooling, supersaturation can lead to nucleation followed by crystal growth. Cloudiness or new solid regions can be consistent with crystallization, but should be verified with experiment context.

title: Precipitation and new solid formation
text: A precipitation process can produce increased turbidity, suspended particles, and eventually settling or a visible solid phase. Similar visual signals can also arise from crystallization, emulsions, bubbles, or poor mixing; reagent identities and solubility context are needed to distinguish them.

title: Liquid-liquid phase separation and settling
text: Immiscible liquid phases can develop a visible interface after mixing. Settling or phase separation is often accompanied by decreasing motion and increasing interface sharpness. Turbidity can decrease as dispersed droplets or particles separate.

title: Dissolution and homogenization
text: Dissolution can be visually associated with decreasing solid-region evidence and decreasing heterogeneity as the mixture becomes more homogeneous. Mixing and temperature can affect the rate. Absence of visible solids does not prove complete molecular dissolution.

title: Color trajectories as reaction/process signals
text: Time-resolved color trajectories can act as observable proxies for process kinetics when chromophores, indicators, oxidation states, or scattering change. A color plateau may indicate visual stabilization but does not by itself prove chemical completion.
